sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anuj Srivastava,Devaang Savla,G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Girish Pandey, Advocate holding brief of Sri Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for the
applicant, Sri Nishant Verma, Advocate holding brief of Sri Anuj Srivastava, learned counsel for the
opposite party no.2 and Sri V.D. Ojha, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.
2.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant- Abhishek Kharwar,
with the prayer to allow this application and quash the entire proceeding as well as impugned charge-sheet dated 10.08.2018 & cognizance/summoning order dated 18.02.2022 in Criminal Case No. 275 of 2022 (State Vs. Abhishek Kharwar) arising out of Case Crime No. 38 of 2018, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 408 I.P.C., Police Station Cantt., District Allahabad, pending in the Abhishek Kharwar vs State Of U.P.And Another on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61256270/
1 court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.17, Allahabad, with a further prayer that proceeding of the aforesaid case be stayed during the pendency of the present application.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the parties have entered into compromise and now no dispute remains between them.

entities.text: Abhishek Kharwar vs State Of U.P.And Another on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While placing paragraph 3, 4 & 5 of the supplementary affidavit dated 22.05.2024 it is submitted that the compromise as entered has been duly verified by the court concerned, page 18 of the said affidavit being the compromise deed and page 16 being the order of the Judicial Magistrate- IV, Prayagraj dated 07.05.2024 verifying the said compromise has been placed before the Court.
4. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 does not dispute the said fact and submits that the dispute between the parties has been settled.
5. Learned counsel for the State could not dispute the fact that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties which was duly verified by the concerned trial court.

6. The law with regards to quashing of a case on the basis of settlement arrived between the parties,
is well settled.

The Apex Court in the cases of (1) B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another: (2003)4 SCC 675; (2) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation : (2008) 9 SCC 677; (3) Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others: ( 2008) 16 SCC 1; (4) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab:
(2012) 10 SCC 303; (5) Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. And another: 2013 (83) ACC 278 and (6) Parbatbhai Ahir@Parbatbhai @ Bhimsinbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another: (2017) 9 SCC 641 has held that the cases in which the parties have settled their grievances can be quashed.

9. The entire proceedings of the said case are hereby quashed subject to the applicant depositing Rs.10,000/- before the concerned trial court which shall be utilized by the District Legal Services Authority of the district.
